subject: Scaling annex: GPU onboarding, prewarm buffer & scale-up lag
messages:
From: Lynn Cho <acme-procurement@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal questions — capacity add-on & latency guarantees

Hi Mina,

We are starting the renewal conversation for our Dedicated deployment (Contract ACME-2024-D). We expect to increase committed capacity for next year and want to lock in behavior around scaling so our production traffic doesn't see cold-start spikes. Specifically, questions:

- Can Redwood guarantee a maximum scale-up lag for buffered/prewarmed GPUs (we're thinking 30s as an upper bound)?
- We want to add 8 additional A100-equivalent GPUs reserved behind the Dedicated contract and keep a small prewarm buffer. Does that change the unit pricing or the commit level?
- Throughput target: sustain 35 concurrent inference requests (avg 512 tokens) with 95th%-tile tail latency <= 300ms. Is that a reasonable throughput SLA for the proposed config?

Also, procurement will need a redline-able annex that spells out min/max replicas, warm-buffer sizing, and an SLA crediting mechanism. Can you share a draft annex we can review?

Thanks,
Lynn
Lynn Cho
Procurement Lead, Acme Retail

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Cho <acme-procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — capacity add-on & latency guarantees

Hi Lynn — thanks for the clear asks. High level response and attached first-pass annex (word). See inline:

- Scale-up lag: We can commit to a 30s P95 scale-up lag for the primary model family (you listed transformer-encoders). Operationally that is achieved via a 2-GPU prewarm buffer plus aggressive warmstart policies. We will include an objective in the annex and a remediation/credit table if P95 exceeds 30s over a monthly window.

- Capacity add: We can reserve +8 GPUs as a committed uplift on top of your current pool. Pricing: the uplift will be priced as a blended reservation rate (we propose a 12% uplift on your current committed rate for the additional reserved units, or an alternative per-GPU monthly flat fee — see annex).

- Throughput SLA: Based on our benchmark for 512-token requests, 35 concurrent requests at 95th percentile <= 300ms is tight but achievable with the proposed config (min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, warm_buffer=2) provided we also enable prefix caching and increase reserved concurrency headroom. We'll put an explicit throughput target and measurement method into the annex.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aditya to validate the benchmark numbers and include a short ops note on caching/warmstart tradeoffs.
2) Marissa to kick off the pricing amendment and confirm billing cadence.
3) I'll put the annex into DocuSign once you confirm the preferred pricing path.

Attaching: ACME_Renewal_Annex_v1.docx and a sample throughput benchmark graph.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Manager — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lynn Cho <acme-procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — capacity add-on & latency guarantees

On Nov 1, 2026, Mina Haddad wrote:
> - Scale-up lag: We can commit to a 30s P95 scale-up lag for the primary model family...

Quick technical note from SE: the 30s P95 is achievable if we accept these operational constraints:

- Warm_buffer strategy: keep 20% of the additional fleet prewarmed during business hours (we recommend 2 GPUs here as Mina proposed). Prewarming is a small hourly cost but avoids cold KV-cache population.
- Min/max replicas: min_replicas=2 ensures baseline capacity for low traffic windows; max_replicas=12 is sized to allow bursts beyond 35 concurrent.
- Scale-up ramp: to avoid noisy slice-by-slice autoscaling, we'll use a fast ramp policy (add 1 replica every 6s, up to 4 replicas immediately) which typically meets the 30s window for the sizes you're planning.
- Monitoring hooks: we'll instrument a synthetic tail-latency probe (1k-token probe) and expose a dashboard; alerting on sustained violations will trigger an operational runbook.

Risks / trade-offs: prewarming increases committed spend by ~3–6% depending on how many GPUs are warm at peak. If Acme prefers to minimize cost we can reduce prewarm to a cold-start fallback + burst buffer, but latency will vary more.

Happy to run a short rerun of the benchmark against Acme's production prompt set; ping me a sample prompt trace if you want that.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lynn Cho <acme-procurement@acme.com>

Thanks Mina/Aditya — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

- We need the annex to include a concrete credit table (example: 5% monthly credit for P95 >30s for >3 production days in the month). Can you propose language?
- Please include a short audit appendix that lists monitoring evidence (dashboards, synthetic probes) and retention period for logs (we require 12 months).
- Pricing: Acme prefers the flat per-GPU monthly uplift option. Please provide the per-GPU number and the alternative blended discount so we can run it through our finance model.

Once we have the annex text and the DocuSign link we will circulate internally and aim to sign by this Friday (2026-11-05).

Regards,
Lynn

Lynn — good plan. Deliverables and owners: 

- Mina: update annex with credit table language (draft below) and upload to DocuSign by EOD 2026-11-04.
  Draft credit language (example): "If the monthly P95 scale-up lag for the production model family exceeds 30 seconds on more than 3 calendar days in the monthly measurement window, Customer will be eligible for a service credit equal to 5% of that month's Dedicated reservation fee for the affected model family. Credits are calculated pro rata and applied to the next invoice."

- Aditya: produce a one-page ops appendix that describes the synthetic probe, data retention (12 months), and the dashboard links. Add a note on the ramp policy (1 replica / 6s, immediate burst to 4 replicas).

- Marissa: provide the per-GPU monthly uplift and the blended 12% uplift schedule; include billing cadence options (monthly vs quarterly invoice).

I've attached the annex v1 and the benchmark graph for your review. When you confirm pricing preference I'll post to DocuSign and include the annex as an amendment to the Master Services Agreement.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference
